svg.title: GLP-1 drugs and atrial fibrillation: what the evidence shows
svg.desc: GLP-1 drugs and atrial fibrillation: what the evidence shows. Newest network meta-analysis (Oct 26, 2026): 94 trials, 155,989 people: injected semaglutide 18% fewer AF reports vs placebo. Verdict: Signal: less AF. Pooled trials in obesity: 24 trials, 40,694 people: 18% fewer AF reports on GLP-1-based drugs. Verdict: Signal: less AF. Heart-outcome trials in diabetes: 8 trials, 60,081 people: no significant change in AF. Verdict: No clear effect. Tirzepatide vs placebo: 10 trials, 6,515 people: AF not significant, wide range; more arrhythmias overall. Verdict: Unclear. Health records: Obesity plus kidney disease: 1.63% vs 2.62% new AF at 1 year on GLP-1 drugs. Verdict: Association only. After AF ablation: 6 mostly observational studies: fewer AF returns on GLP-1 drugs. Verdict: Low certainty. Heart rate (FDA labels): Resting heart rate rises 1 to 4 beats a minute on average. Verdict: Known effect. Trials powered for AF: None of 249 drug trials; placebo trials in people with AF due 2026-27. Verdict: Not yet done.
